title: Refunds, repairs and replacements
log: 2026-11-20T12:15:12Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new
2026-11-20T12:25:40Z write: the API refused it in the chapter request, so it is written on its own next

match.reason: The bank card says a consumer can always choose a repair, replacement or refund, but the new point teaches that a major fault gives the consumer the choice of refund or replacement while a minor fault lets the business repair first, a rule the card does not cover.

draft.title: Refunds, repairs and replacements
card: If goods fail a consumer guarantee, the Australian Consumer Law gives the buyer a remedy. The remedy depends on whether the fault is major or minor.
a serious problem, such as one that makes the goods unsafe or means a reasonable buyer would not have bought them. The consumer chooses a refund or a replacement.
a smaller problem that can be fixed. The business chooses whether to repair the goods, replace them or give a refund. Usually the business fixes it first.
If a business does not fix a minor fault in a reasonable time, the consumer can then ask for a refund or replacement. A store cannot refuse just because it has a "no refunds" sign.
draft.remember: Major fault: the consumer chooses refund or replacement. Minor fault: the business can repair first.

a.q: Who chooses between a refund and a replacement when goods have a major fault?
a.why: For a major fault, the consumer picks a refund or a replacement. The business picks only for a minor fault, where it can choose to repair the goods first.
a.clue: Think about who gets the choice when the fault is serious.

b.q: Priya buys a pair of headphones in Penrith. A week later the left speaker crackles, but they still work. The store offers to repair them. What is the best description of this?
opts: A minor fault, so the store may repair first
A major fault, so Priya must get a refund
A minor fault, so Priya must accept a refund
A major fault, so the store may repair first
b.why: The headphones still work and the problem can be fixed, so it is a minor fault. The business can choose to repair first. It would be a major fault only if the problem were serious, and then Priya would choose.
b.clue: The headphones still work and can be fixed.

b.best: A minor fault, so the store may repair first
